verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.title: Canine Thorax · Lateral + Annotated VHS Example
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.credit: Original radiograph: Ophélie TISSIER; annotated version by Uwe Gille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

images.caption: Unannotated lateral thoracic image; side of recumbency and normality not established by source.
Derivative of this canine thoracic radiograph with vertebral heart score markings.

verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.history: Source image shows a large dog in lateral recumbency; patient complaint and final diagnosis not provided.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.quality: Check thoracic field coverage, respiratory phase, sternum/spine overlap, exposure, and positioning.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.findings: Identify cardiac silhouette and vertebral bodies. The annotated derivative demonstrates a vertebral heart score measurement concept; it is not a validated clinical conclusion about this patient.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.interpretation: Anatomy and VHS technique reference. A vertebral heart score should be interpreted with breed, age, projection and clinical context.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.differentials: Not assigned; source does not establish a disease.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.why: The VHS method expresses long- and short-axis heart silhouette dimensions relative to thoracic vertebral length; interpretation depends on species/breed and acquisition.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.next: Practice identifying measurement axes on the original view, then check the annotated derivative. Correlate a measured score with patient context.

verified-canine-thorax-vd.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-thorax-vd.title: Canine Thorax · Ventrodorsal Reference

images.caption: Ventro-dorsal projection from a large dog; do not assume the same animal as the lateral example.

verified-canine-thorax-vd.history: Large dog; clinical history not specified.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.quality: Assess centering, thoracic symmetry/rotation, lung coverage, laterality and exposure indicator if available.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.findings: Practice identifying right and left lung fields, cardiac silhouette, diaphragm, ribs and mediastinum.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.interpretation: Projection recognition reference; radiographic normality is not independently confirmed.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.differentials: No source-confirmed diagnosis; avoid inventing one.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.why: VD beam travel is ventral to dorsal. Rotation distorts the appearance of bilateral thoracic structures.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.next: Use alongside a true patient-matched lateral view whenever making clinical interpretations.

verified-feline-thorax-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.title: Feline Thorax · Age-Related Bronchial Wall Mineralization
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.credit: AurelioAHeckert · Public domain dedication (Commons file description)

images.caption: The source report describes normal-sized cardiac silhouette and mineralized bronchial walls; view side not established.

verified-feline-thorax-lateral.history: Female domestic cat; report in source describes age-related bronchial wall calcification, without additional clinical history.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.quality: Confirm entire thorax included, correct projection/markers and adequate inspiration.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.findings: Source interpretation: heart silhouette within normal parameters; bronchial wall calcification described as a senile change; no radiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary metastasis in the views studied.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.interpretation: Source-reported bronchial wall calcification; no radiographic metastatic pattern reported. This is not equivalent to excluding all lung disease.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.differentials: Bronchial mineralization may be age-related; assess for concurrent inflammatory airway patterns with clinical correlation.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.why: Mineralized bronchial walls can create conspicuous ring/tram-line opacities; recognize chronic or age-related changes without automatically diagnosing active bronchitis.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.next: Correlate with respiratory history, prior imaging and orthogonal views.

verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.title: Feline Abdomen · Normal GI Appearance + T13–L1 Spondylosis

images.caption: Source describes GI tract as apparently normal and T13–L1 spondylosis.

verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.history: Source: 12-year-old overweight (BCS 6/9) castrated male cat imaged for suspected swallowed bone.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.quality: Check abdominal coverage and positioning; single-view examinations have limitations.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.findings: The source describes gastrointestinal appearance as unremarkable but notes spondylosis between T13 and L1.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.interpretation: No obvious GI finding described in this source image; T13–L1 spondylosis is a distinct radiographic finding.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.differentials: Clinical gastrointestinal obstruction may still warrant further evaluation; spondylosis may be incidental.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.why: Spondylosis involves degenerative osseous bridging/osteophytes, which may be unrelated to the presenting digestive complaint.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.next: Correlate with examination and additional imaging if clinical concern persists.

verified-canine-gdv-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.title: Canine GDV · Lateral Abdominal Radiograph

images.caption: Source-identified side-view X-ray of gastric dilatation–volvulus (GDV).

verified-canine-gdv-lateral.history: The source identifies a canine GDV radiograph but supplies no complete clinical signalment.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.quality: Check that the distended stomach and relevant abdomen are included; side of lateral projection is not provided.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.findings: Assess gastric distension and abnormal intragastric gas compartmentalization suggestive of volvulus. Identify the gas/fluid pattern from the actual view.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.interpretation: Source-labeled example of canine gastric dilatation–volvulus.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.differentials: Simple gastric distension and alternative gastric outflow problems; interpret with clinical status.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.why: Gastric torsion can occlude venous outflow and compromise perfusion; time-critical shock and tissue injury can develop.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.next: Emergency stabilization and immediate veterinary surgical assessment; do not delay lifesaving care for additional views.

verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.title: Equine Laminitis · Annotated P3 Rotation
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.credit: Malcolm Morley (radiograph), Froggerlaura (annotations) · public domain (Commons file description)

images.caption: P2 and P3 labeled; yellow/white distance lines demonstrate change in dorsal hoof-wall-to-P3 relationship.

verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.history: Source describes a laminitic horse foot, without full individual history.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.quality: Original annotation is part of the image. Later unannotated views may be added to the same case.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.findings: The source identifies an increased distance between the distal portion of P3 and the dorsal hoof wall, indicating displacement/rotation in the laminitic example.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.interpretation: Annotated source-identified laminitis with distal phalanx rotation relative to the hoof wall.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.differentials: Other causes of hoof pain or altered phalangeal alignment require clinical and radiographic correlation.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.why: Damage to the lamellar suspension of P3 can allow its position within the hoof capsule to change.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.next: Interpret with lameness findings and standardized farriery/radiographic measurements; assess urgent support and treatment.

verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.title: Feline Cystolith · Source-Labeled Struvite Stone
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.lecture: Diagnostic Imaging · Small Animal Abdomen / Urology

images.view: Feline urinary bladder radiograph · projection not stated
images.caption: Source explicitly labels a struvite bladder stone in a cat. Stone composition cannot be reliably identified by radiographic opacity alone.

verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.credit: Bludwar · Public-domain dedication on Wikimedia Commons
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.history: Wikimedia source identifies a feline struvite bladder stone; signalment and diagnostic confirmation method are not supplied.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.lookFor: Find the urinary bladder region; look for a mineral-opaque focus within its expected lumen. Ask whether location is confirmed on an orthogonal projection.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.quality: Original source does not establish the projection name. Confirm correct anatomical positioning and projection marker before interpreting.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.findings: Source-labeled mineral opacity compatible with a bladder calculus; verify the position relative to the expected urinary bladder and surrounding pelvis.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.interpretation: Source-reported feline cystolith, described by its author as struvite. Radiography alone is not sufficient to establish stone composition.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.differentials: Radiopaque urolith, mineralized soft tissue outside the bladder, or superimposed fecal/other mineral opacity; localization from orthogonal images is important.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.why: Calcium-containing and some magnesium-ammonium-phosphate calculi can be radiopaque. Opacity, shape and position inform the workup but do not confirm chemistry.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.next: Urinalysis, urine culture when indicated, imaging in another plane, and composition analysis where available.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.reviewStatus: Source-described finding; chemical composition is attributed to original uploader, not independently proven by X-ray.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.imageStatus: Original Commons file linked, rights and description verified

verified-canine-cystolith-overview.title: Canine Urinary Bladder Stones · Abdominal Study
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.lecture: Diagnostic Imaging · Small Animal Abdomen / Urology

images.caption: Joel Mills original photograph of a canine radiograph showing bladder stones.

verified-canine-cystolith-overview.history: Original image described as a canine radiograph showing bladder stones; no age, breed or clinical complaint supplied.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.lookFor: Identify the bladder silhouette/expected location; count mineral opacities, describe margins, and note whether the urethra is fully included.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.quality: The source does not specify projection or diagnostic technique, and this is a photograph of a displayed radiograph.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.findings: Original photographer identifies urinary bladder stones. Describe number, size, mineral opacity and location rather than assuming composition.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.interpretation: Source-identified canine cystoliths; size/composition should not be inferred without further examination.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.differentials: Bladder calculi versus extravesical mineral opacity or superposition. Consider possible urethral urolithiasis if clinical obstruction is suspected.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.why: Urinary calculi result from crystallization/aggregation under permissive urinary conditions. Some are radiopaque and some may be radiolucent.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.next: Combine with urinalysis, culture when indicated and urinary ultrasound or complementary projections; evaluate urinary outflow urgently if obstructed.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.imageStatus: Original Commons file linked, rights and description verified

verified-canine-gdv-second-source.title: Canine GDV · Compartmentalization and Pyloric Displacement
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.lecture: Diagnostic Imaging · Small Animal Abdomen / Emergency

images.caption: Original source notes abnormal cranial positioning of pylorus/duodenum and gastric double-bubble compartmentalization.

verified-canine-gdv-second-source.history: Large mixed-breed dog; original photographer describes gastric dilatation–volvulus.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.lookFor: Identify the distended gas-filled stomach, then look for separation into gas compartments and abnormal pyloric location. How does this differ from simple gastric dilation?
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.quality: Check cranial abdominal coverage. This is a photograph of a radiograph; projection side is not established in source.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.findings: Original source: trapped gas distends stomach; displaced pylorus and duodenum appear cranial to stomach, with a separating gastric fold ('double bubble').
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.interpretation: Source-confirmed canine GDV image, demonstrating compartmentalization and abnormal pyloric position.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.differentials: Simple gastric dilatation without volvulus; other causes of distension or gastric outflow dysfunction.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.why: Rotation obstructs normal gastric transit and may compromise venous drainage, leading to rapid gastric distension, ischemia and cardiovascular compromise.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.next: Immediate stabilization and surgical assessment; do not delay emergency treatment for unnecessary additional imaging.
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.imageStatus: Original Commons file linked, rights and description verified
verified-canine-gdv-second-source.reviewStatus: Uploader-described teaching record; not a specialist-reviewed diagnosis

verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.title: Equine Laminitis · Radiographic Measurement Guide

images.caption: Source annotation labels CE, HL, SD, DB, and PA radiographic measurement concepts.

verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.history: Original creator presents annotated measurements relevant to assessing laminitis; individual patient signalment is not specified.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.lookFor: Find P3, the dorsal hoof wall, the solar surface and the coronary band. What each line measures is more important than memorizing a value from this single image.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.quality: Annotated educational reference, not an independent clinical measurement from a supplied case history.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.findings: CE = coronary extensor distance; HL = horn–lamellar distance; SD = sole depth; DB = digital breakover; PA = palmar angle, per original figure description.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.interpretation: Radiographic measurement teaching guide for monitoring structural effects of laminitis. Annotations do not alone establish individual severity.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.differentials: Differentiate hoof capsule conformation and positioning effects from actual distal phalanx displacement using standardized technique and clinical context.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.why: Loss of integrity of the suspensory lamellae can permit displacement of P3, alter sole depth and change the relationship between dorsal hoof wall and bone.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.next: Use standardized marker placement and consistent limb positioning; compare serial radiographs with veterinary and farrier findings.

verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.title: Feline Thorax · Projection & Anatomy Reference

images.view: Feline thoracic radiograph · source does not specify projection
images.caption: Source caption states feline thoracic radiograph without a diagnosis or projection label.

verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.history: No clinical history or radiographic diagnosis provided by the original uploader.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.lookFor: Identify cardiac silhouette, trachea, diaphragm, ribs and visible lungs. Before naming a view, check the actual orientation and side markers.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.quality: Projection and inspiration/rotation must be assessed from the image; original uploader does not specify diagnostic quality.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.findings: Study anatomy and the region included. Do not assume that the image is disease-free because the uploader provided no diagnosis.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.interpretation: Anatomy and projection-recognition exercise; NOT independently verified as a normal feline thorax.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.differentials: No confirmed source diagnosis; if abnormalities are suspected, describe them objectively and consult an appropriately qualified interpreter.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.why: Feline thoracic conformation differs from dogs, and projection, respiratory phase and positioning can all change radiographic appearance.
verified-feline-thorax-source-reference.next: Practice comparing the image with annotated feline thoracic anatomy from approved course sources.
